messages:
maria: quick heads-up — spotted a subtle regression after the embeddings model swap. starting a thread to coordinate docs fixes + a tiny snippet for clients.
alex: what regression? any customer hits?
devon: internal tests: when runtime falls back from redwood-embed-2 to redwood-embed-lite, returned vector dims differ (1536 vs 512). clients that assumed fixed dims end up with padded/truncated arrays. reproducible with long documents.
maria: exact symptom: client-side code expects 1536 dims; fallback to 512 led to silent padding which broke nearest-neighbor lookups.
jin: we should add a short compatibility table and a snippet that detects dims on first call and fails fast or reindexes. small PR.
sam: agreed. also add a deprecation note: v1 API implicitly masked dims; v2 requires explicit model choice/awareness.
devon: i've prepared TS + Py guard snippets and a minimal repro. gist will go in the PR.
maria: proposed python snippet for docs: 
```
# check embedding size once and fail/convert if unexpected
resp = client.embeddings.create(model=\"redwood-embed-2\", input=[text])
dim = len(resp.data[0].embedding)
if dim != EXPECTED_DIM:
    raise RuntimeError(f\"Unexpected embed dim {dim}. reindex or pin model variant.\")
```
alex: add a note about routing policies: if customers allow runtime fallback, they must pin model_id for index-critical calls. include example.
jenna: also add a compact one-line callout at the top of the migration guide: \"If your app assumes fixed embedding dimensions, pin an embedding model or reindex during swaps.\" keep it short and visible.
sam: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4021 — includes table, snippets, FAQ. request reviews.
alex: I'll review. tiny lint nit: include v1->v2 mapping row with dim deltas. add a CLI reindex example.
devon: CLI suggestion for reindexing: 
```
# simple reindex CLI
python reindex_embeddings.py --src-index old_index --model redwood-embed-2
```
jin: add a short \"Preprocessing & tokenization caveats\" section — whitespace/tokenization differences can change embedding outputs and near-duplicate detection. link to tokenizer notes.
maria: good call. add bullets for normalization, punctuation handling, and language-specific quirks.
sam: added a test in the PR that simulates fallback and asserts explicit error when strict_mode=true.
alex: LGTM except one request: include a structured server log example so customers can triage when fallback occurs.
devon: logging example: 
```
{\"event\":\"embed_fallback\",\"requested_model\":\"redwood-embed-2\",\"served_model\":\"redwood-embed-lite\",\"dim_expected\":1536,\"dim_actual\":512}
```
(use structured JSON in logs)
jenna: i'll add the deprecation banner markup and a short release-notes blurb: \"Embedding vector dims may change during model swaps — see migration guide.\"
maria: can we ship today? this will help customers with large indices.
sam: i'll mark the PR high-priority and request eng-runtime + devex reviews. ping those teams in PR description.
alex: assigned a docs reviewer and added owners check.
devon: i'll run post-merge QA: reindex a sample corpus and sanity-check knn scores.
docs-bot: PR 4021 merged into main by sam — congratulations! :tada:
maria: great — follow-up: schedule a brief QA run next week and publish a short note in the changelog.
alex: noted. assigning QA run to devon.
devon: on it — will run reindex and report any drift.
maria: thanks all. this should reduce surprise outages for customers relying on fixed dims.
